label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: deck sent ruv-sgit its second experiment and had it back within the hour
findings.why: Deck, ruv-sgit, dev and the designer are named as if known, and one sentence strings five happenings together, so a phone reader in a gap between meetings cannot tell who does what.

findings.quote: nobody started any work but the clock
findings.why: Good hook, but the chapter never says early what a team of this kind can copy from it, so the takeaway waits until the closing card.

findings.quote: What the record shows is not whether everything finished
findings.why: This reports what the record shows rather than saying what I, the editor, make of it now, with hindsight.

findings.quote: A request not picked up at one session is picked up at the next. Nobody chased it.
findings.why: Short flat sentences in a row announce the lesson instead of letting one thought run.

findings.quote: Part four keeps all three, and asks what that order should have been.
findings.why: A pointer forward to a question the reader has not yet been given the means to ask.

findings.quote: Three rounds, one picture, and I started none of them.
findings.why: The three rounds were just told in the preceding sentences and the figure shows them again.

findings.quote: answered at the next and used at the one after, with nobody chasing it
findings.why: The same 'nobody chased it' point was made at lines 34 and 71, and the record note says it is told in chapter 10.

findings.quote: Hours of work nobody started, and what it had produced was a queue only I could clear.
findings.why: This is the strongest finding for a team with a central person, the exact deal-breaker, yet it is a passing line and not weighed against the claim that a team can run alone.

findings.quote: Nine hours, then, with every wake started by the clock and nothing tidied away
findings.why: The closing summary restates the chapter's opening and the partial-wake point already made twice.

findings.quote: the temptation is to start asking straight away.
findings.why: It presumes the reader's temptation, and the card is too thin to start from tomorrow: it names no first step.

findings.quote: What your own team can take from them is the same at every stop
findings.why: A promise that each stop carries a takeaway, but the stops are mostly descriptions of pages with an invented one-line quote.

findings.quote: And it fits on an iPad.
findings.why: A dev quote that tells a team member nothing about running a team.

findings.quote: frame by frame, with the source of every number in it
findings.why: Thirteen stops of page tours are a long walk for a busy reader; the animations and maps are about the talk, not the team's method.

findings.quote: The **blind team**, the Cold-Read team, read the talk's record
findings.why: Internal team names with a long sentence in a glossary; an outsider needs a plainer line.

findings.quote: Nothing here is new: each line is the book's own.
findings.why: Tells the reader about the glossary's provenance, which they do not need.

what_holds: 09-nine-hours-with-nobody-starting-work.md: the partial wake that says it is partial, and the empty mailroom with everything waiting on the editor, are the honest, copyable pattern a team would want, and the lapse left in builds trust.
90-the-tour-at-length.md: short stops with a figure and one line each are easy to dip into on a phone.
91-the-words-used.md: plain one-line definitions of agent, wake, scope, hold and board that I could hand to my own team.
notes: The chapter 9 picture of the schedule is the most useful thing for my team, but the takeaway about the central queue is buried. Synthetic reader only.
